sugestoes.texto: The asynchronous legacy write inherits cancellation from the HTTP request context despite its new ten-second timeout. Once the response completes, request cancellation can abort the legacy operation or cause it to start with an already-cancelled context, leaving successful unified writes unreplicated; the same defect affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) so namespace and identity values survive without inheriting request cancellation.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than a wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. playlist legacyStorage.Update calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) on its own legacy object, so a patch is recalculated against potentially stale legacy state and can fail or persist a different result from the successful unified update. Restore updateWrapper with updated: res for the legacy call.

Successful Delete records the resource name in the histogram's kind label instead of options.Kind. metrics.go passes this value directly into the global HistogramVec, retaining a separate histogram for every distinct deleted object name and causing memory and exported-series growth as resources churn. Pass options.Kind consistently with the error path and other operations.

The successful Update test only checks the returned unified-store object, while both backends share the same mock and identical Update expectations. There is no condition that waits for and verifies the legacy write. Deleting the Legacy.Update goroutine entirely would still pass this test; the Create test has the same blind spot. Use separate backend mocks and a completion signal for the legacy invocation, then verify its arguments and call count after completion so these tests actually distinguish mode 3 from storage-only writes.

This case says creation happens only in the unified store, but it sets up Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create explicitly launches that legacy write after Storage.Create succeeds. The test output therefore describes the opposite of the dual-write behavior being exercised; name it as a write to both stores.

The case description says listing is not implemented, but this PR implements List by delegating to Storage.List. This case merely returns errors.New("error") from that mock and checks propagation; it does not simulate or assert an unimplemented-operation error. Rename it to describe a unified-store listing failure so test reports do not incorrectly imply Mode3 lacks List support.

The legacy write now runs after the method returns, but its timeout still inherits the request context. When the HTTP handler finishes, that context is canceled; a legacy call scheduled afterward (or still doing database work) therefore fails despite a successful unified write. This affects Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection and can systematically leave the stores inconsistent. Detach request cancellation while preserving context values before starting the bounded background work, or complete the write before returning.

Returning before the legacy update finishes removes ordering even for sequential client requests. Update A can commit to unified storage and return, then update B commits and its legacy goroutine runs first; A's delayed legacy goroutine can subsequently overwrite B (or B can fail a version check), leaving legacy storage with A while unified storage contains B. Create followed by Delete can similarly run legacy Delete before legacy Create and resurrect a deleted object. Preserve commit ordering for background writes per resource, or keep these writes synchronous.

This branch follows Storage.Create, but records a legacy duration even though no legacy call occurs. The same copy-paste error occurs in the Storage.Update error branch at line 129. Consequently storage failures disappear from storage metrics and falsely inflate legacy failures and timings. Use recordStorageDuration in both storage error branches.

Every other duration emission, including this method's error branch and legacy call, passes options.Kind in this position. Passing name on success splits success and failure measurements across different kind values and creates a separate metric series for each deleted object. Pass options.Kind consistently.

This timing surrounds Legacy.DeleteCollection, but emits through recordStorageDuration. A successful collection deletion therefore emits two storage measurements and no legacy measurement; a legacy failure is also incorrectly reported as a storage failure. Record this call with recordLegacyDuration.

The preceding line enriches log with name, kind and method, but the context receives d.Log instead. Storage and legacy code retrieving the context logger therefore lose those operation fields, unlike the other methods. Install log in the context.

Create now returns before Legacy.Create completes, but the goroutine derives its timeout from the original request context. HTTP request contexts are canceled when the handler returns, so a successful primary write can immediately cancel its legacy mirror, leaving the stores inconsistent. The same mismatch affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Detach cancellation while preserving request values (for example with context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before applying the bounded timeout, or retain synchronous completion.

Previously Legacy.Update received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update. Passing the original objInfo instead makes the legacy consumer invoke UpdatedObject against its own old object. For patches or transforms, especially when legacy data is stale, this can produce a different object (or fail on a patch precondition) despite the primary update succeeding. Preserve the wrapper with updated: res so the legacy write mirrors the committed primary result rather than independently evaluating the update.

issues.descricao: Delete puts the base d.Log instead of the enriched per-call logger into the context, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method fields.
issues.textoGolden: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

comentarios.texto: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` installs the mode-level logger instead of the request-scoped `log` built on line 96 (which carries name, kind and method) — a copy/paste error, as every other method in this file passes the composed `log`. Storage.Delete and the legacy delete goroutine therefore log without the per-request fields this PR is adding (and without the metrics method/kind context).
ctx is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of the enriched `log`. The delete logs then lose the name, kind and method values. Use `log`.
The Delete context uses d.Log rather than the per-call log. This is a logging-context inconsistency (not a data leak); use the per-call logger for consistency.

issues.descricao: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
issues.textoGolden: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

comentarios.texto: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

issues.descricao: Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

comentarios.texto: The Delete success-path metric passes `name` where every other call site in this file (lines 48, 103, 113, 156, 159) passes options.Kind in the kind/name argument slot. The storage-success sample for Delete is thus labelled with the object name instead of the resource kind, breaking label consistency with the other operations and with the error sample emitted at line 103. Use options.Kind here (or insert name consistently everywhere, matching the metric's label semantics).
recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) at line 106 passes the object name in the kind label slot.

recordStorageDuration is called with the object `name` as the `kind` label: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. Every other storage call site passes `options.Kind` (lines 73, 89, 103, 156, 159). This injects a per-object value into the kind label, corrupting the metric and giving it unbounded cardinality (one series per object name), which grows memory on every delete. Should be `options.Kind`.

issues.descricao: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

comentarios.texto: On a Storage.Create failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) — the failing subsystem is Storage, not Legacy, and it passes the storage start time. This records storage failures under the legacy metric, corrupting the dual-writer error dashboards (and contradicts the success path on line 48 which uses recordStorageDuration). Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

On a Storage.Update failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), attributing a storage failure and its storage duration to the legacy metric. This is inconsistent with the success path on line 132 (recordStorageDuration) and with mode1's semantics. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

The async goroutine performing the LEGACY DeleteCollection measures it with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Every other legacy write in this file uses recordLegacyDuration (lines 56, 113, 140); recording it under the storage metric reports legacy latency/errors as storage latency/errors. Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

issues.descricao: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

comentarios.texto: The async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns — which is immediately after Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return — so the goroutine's Legacy.Create can be canceled before completing, silently dropping the legacy write that this mode exists to guarantee. The same applies to the goroutines at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Detach the async context from request cancellation (e.g. derive from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background()) before applying the timeout.

The legacy write in Mode 3 became fire-and-forget, changing the contract callers relied on: previously Create (and, identically, Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) returned only after the LegacyStorage call had been made in-request; now it returns immediately and the write runs in a detached goroutine. Worse, the goroutine builds its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), which the API server cancels as soon as the handler returns/flushes the response — so the legacy write and its 10s timeout will typically be cancelled outright and the legacy store silently stops being updated, which is precisely what the new mode-3 integration cases assume still happens. Any detached work must be given a context not tied to the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a server-lifetime context), and consumers that depended on the synchronous legacy write need to be updated.

The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

issues.descricao: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.

comentarios.texto: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Restore forwarding of the committed result via updateWrapper instead of recomputing the update against legacy state.

issues.descricao: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

comentarios.texto: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

issues.descricao: The List error test case is still named 'not implemented' although List is now implemented and the case checks storage error propagation.

comentarios.texto: The test-case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" still describes the old stub List (which returned nil, nil with a "List not implemented" log). List is now implemented at dualwriter_mode3.go:79 and delegates to Storage.List; the case merely checks that a Storage error is propagated. The name contradicts the code it now exercises — rename it, e.g. "error when listing objects in the unified store fails".

issues.descricao: The Create test case name says 'only in the unified store' although Mode 3 also writes to legacy.

comentarios.texto: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

issues.descricao: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

comentarios.texto: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

issues.descricao: The storage-failure Create test registers its failing expectation via setupLegacyFn and only works because legacy and storage share one mock.

comentarios.texto: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers the failing Create expectation only through setupLegacyFn. It passes only because legacy and storage share one mock, so the storage Create gets that error by accident. Register the expectation in setupStorageFn and use separate mocks for legacy and storage, so the test really covers a storage failure.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.

comentarios.texto: Assertions that can never fail. `assert.Equal(t, obj, exampleObj)` compares the value the shared mock was configured to return (`m.On("Delete", ...).Return(exampleObj, false, nil)` at line 202) against that same fixture, so it restates the stub rather than exercising anything; `assert.NotEqual(t, obj, anotherObj)` compares against a different fixture value and is true for every possible return of `dw.Delete`, including `nil`. Either assertion would still pass if the storage call were removed and `nil, 0, nil` returned. The same pair (Equal-against-fixture + NotEqual-against-other-fixture) is repeated at lines 129-130, 183-184, 291-292 and 352-353 in the other tests. Assert something the code actually produces, e.g. that the name/argument passed through to the storage mock matches the input (`us.AssertCalled(t, "Delete", mock.Anything, tt.input, mock.Anything, mock.Anything)`) or assert on the returned error/async flag.

issues.descricao: Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.

comentarios.texto: Goroutine captures mutable obj/options while caller returns object that can alias it; DeepCopy before handing to goroutine to avoid concurrent read/write race.

issues.descricao: Empty comment.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The header conditional ends with `end if`, leaving a Ruby modifier without a condition. WHY: Rendering the best template raises a syntax error instead of displaying comments for any existing embedded topic. HOW: Close the conditional with `end` alone.

WHAT: Feed content extraction assumes every entry has a `content` field. WHY: SimpleRSS exposes RSS `description` and `content:encoded` separately, so ordinary RSS entries without Atom-style `content` abort the entire poll when `scrub` is called on nil (or the missing field accessor fails). HOW: Select the available content, content:encoded, or description field before scrubbing, and handle entries with no body explicitly.

WHAT: Imported feed HTML is stored using raw_html cooking without sanitization. WHY: PollFeed passes decoded feed content to this method, absolutize_urls only parses and rewrites URLs, and Post.cook returns the HTML unchanged, allowing feed-supplied script elements or event handlers to execute under the forum origin when the post is viewed. HOW: Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe element, attribute, and URL-scheme allowlist before storing or returning it as cooked HTML.

WHAT: Every uncached embed URL triggers a complete feed fetch and import pass. WHY: The retrieval throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so requests for different articles or query variants each download the same feed and iterate all entries, multiplying network and database work on background workers instead of retaining the hourly polling bound. HOW: Use a shared feed-level throttle or lock to bound polling across retrieval jobs, and fall back to fetching the requested article when polling is skipped.

WHAT: The URL absolutizer only handles leading slashes and treats protocol-relative URLs as same-host paths. WHY: Links such as `images/photo.jpg` remain relative to the forum rather than the source article, while `//cdn.example/image.jpg` becomes a path on the article host, producing broken imported links and images. HOW: Resolve non-absolute href and src values against the full source URL using URI resolution rather than concatenating the host prefix.

The changed EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) when no embed exists, but this test still requires TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve during the request. With jobs queued rather than executed inline, those expectations are never fulfilled and the controller spec fails despite the controller following its new asynchronous contract. Assert the enqueue call here and test retriever invocation in the job spec instead.

Valid RSS feeds commonly put article text in description rather than content. For those items i.content is nil, so calling scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll (with retry disabled). Select the available content/description field and handle items without either before invoking String methods.

The existence lookup occurs before this transaction and does not serialize imports. Two workers importing the same URL can both see no embed and create a post; the second TopicEmbed.create! then raises on the unique embed_url index. This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps a retrieve job, since polling bypasses the retrieval throttle. The transaction prevents a committed duplicate post but does not prevent the unhandled exception and aborted feed poll. Serialize imports per URL or rescue the uniqueness conflict outside the transaction and load the winning embed.

Each negative example leaves the other prerequisites at their defaults (polling disabled and URL/username empty). Consequently, removing the URL guard or username guard from execute still passes its corresponding test because the earlier polling-enabled guard stops execution; removing the enabled guard also remains masked by the empty URL. Set all three settings to valid enabled values in a before block, then override only the setting being tested in each example.

This request does not configure an embeddable host or valid referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects it before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). The non-success assertion therefore still passes if required-parameter validation is removed entirely, and it does not verify the claimed 404 either. Configure the host and matching referer for this example and assert the intended missing-parameter response specifically.

The URL is interpolated into both an HTML attribute and text without escaping. The http(s) prefix check does not reject quotes or markup: a feed link containing an apostrophe can introduce attributes, and markup in the URL can become elements. Nokogiri parsing in absolutize_urls is not sanitization, and raw_html cooking preserves the resulting markup for readers. Escape the URL in both contexts before constructing the attribution.

Unlike the translated controls in this template, the visible post date uses strftime with a fixed order and English abbreviated month names. Non-English forums therefore display English dates even when the surrounding embed labels are translated. Use the localization helper so the active locale controls the month names and date format.

The opening `if @topic_view.posts.present?` must close with `end`, not `end if`. ERB compiles this into Ruby with a dangling `if` modifier, producing a syntax error. Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of displaying comments (regardless of whether posts are present).

issues.descricao: The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.textoGolden: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

comentarios.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.descricao: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.descricao: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.textoGolden: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.descricao: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.textoGolden: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

comentarios.texto: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

comentarios.texto: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.descricao: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

comentarios.texto: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.descricao: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

comentarios.texto: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.descricao: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

comentarios.texto: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.descricao: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.descricao: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

comentarios.texto: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.descricao: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

comentarios.texto: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.descricao: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

comentarios.texto: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` result is used unguarded via `comments.appendChild`. WHY: pages including the script without the placeholder throw TypeError and abort embedding.

issues.descricao: Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.

comentarios.texto: The controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and never instantiates `TopicRetriever`, but spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (lines 40-46, also added by this PR) declares the opposite contract for this action: it sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` and then expects the `best` request to satisfy those mocks. Because the request path only enqueues a Sidekiq job (which is not executed inline here), `TopicRetriever.new` is never called during `get :best`, so the expectation is unmet and the 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' example fails. The two hunks encode two different interfaces for the same retrieval trigger; align them (either have the controller call TopicRetriever directly, or update the spec to stub `Jobs.enqueue`/run the job inline).

Spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve but EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...) instead; the mock never matches so the test fails. Update the spec to expect the enqueue (or the job) to match the controller's async contract.

Update this test to expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: nil, embed_url: embed_url), rather than synchronous TopicRetriever construction and retrieval. EmbedController#best now only enqueues the job; those calls occur in Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute. Consequently these mock expectations are unsatisfied during the controller request under normal asynchronous execution, causing the new controller spec to fail. Test retriever construction separately at the job boundary.

issues.descricao: The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: poll_feed fetches and re-imports the entire feed hourly via `open(feed_url)` with `feed_key` never used for conditional GET. WHY: every hour downloads full feed and runs a DB transaction per item even when unchanged, causing O(N) network/DB blowup with large feeds.
feed_key is computed but never read by execute/poll_feed; polling therefore never uses conditional-GET/throttle key and re-imports every hour. Wire feed_key into poll_feed or remove it.

issues.descricao: States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: The fallback on nil/empty/non-http is correct and re-guarded in import.

issues.descricao: States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: The comparison `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` is safe because Discourse's Enum is 1-based.

issues.descricao: States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: `present?` is used explicitly rather than raw truthiness, and enum values are >= 1, so :regular is still set.

issues.descricao: States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: `if topic_id` is safe because topic ids are >= 1, never 0.

issues.descricao: Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.

comentarios.texto: Lines 25-26 use blank?/!=.

issues.descricao: States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: `content_sha1` uses string compare and `absolutize_urls` is correct; the port guard and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` indices are correct.

issues.descricao: States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.

comentarios.texto: Uses setnx boolean and explicit no_throttle check.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.

comentarios.texto: `open(url)` is called with a URL that comes from the embed_url request parameter and from RSS item links, and the scheme is never validated. With open-uri, Kernel#open can run commands for strings starting with `|` and can read local files. Validate that the scheme is http/https and use `URI.parse(url).open` or Net::HTTP.

issues.descricao: Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
issues.textoGolden: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

issues.descricao: Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
issues.textoGolden: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the if/else block opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby (`if` cannot be a modifier on `end`). WHY: Erubis/ERB compiles this tag into Ruby and the resulting SyntaxError causes every render of the embed 'best' view to raise, so the entire embedded-comments feature fails to load. HOW: change line 6 to `<%- end %>` to match the `if` from line 2.

The `if` opened at line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>` at line 6. The dangling `if` has no condition, so the compiled ERB (`... else ... end if`) is invalid Ruby and raises SyntaxError when the template is compiled — `embed/best` will fail to render at all rather than showing the comments. Change line 6 to a bare `<%- end %>`.

The header conditional ends with `end if`, leaving a modifier `if` without a condition in the generated Ruby template. Rendering any existing embedded topic fails with a template syntax error instead of displaying comments. Replace this tag with `<%- end %>`.

issues.descricao: The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
issues.textoGolden: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

comentarios.texto: `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into an inline script string. A referer on the allowed host with a single quote in its path can break out of the string and run script (XSS). Build the target origin from the validated URI (scheme://host[:port]) and output it with `to_json`/`j`.

issues.descricao: Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
issues.textoGolden: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: parent.postMessage targetOrigin uses full `request.referer` (including path/query, possibly nil/attacker-controlled). WHY: targetOrigin must be an origin, so a full URL never matches and resize messages are dropped (nil referer throws), breaking auto-resize.

postMessage targetOrigin uses request.referer (full URL with path) but receiver validates e.origin (scheme+host+port). Full URL never equals origin so resize message is blocked/mismatched. Send only the origin to agree with embed.js check.

issues.descricao: Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
issues.textoGolden: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

issues.descricao: Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.

comentarios.texto: Migration defaults cook_method to 1 but Post.cook_methods is Enum(:regular,:raw_html) so 0=regular,1=raw_html. Default becomes raw_html, so Post#cook returns raw uncooked for all existing/new posts by default, bypassing sanitization. Change default to 0 (regular).

issues.descricao: Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.

comentarios.texto: The 'not a url' test does not stub embeddable_host. The blank default never matches any host, so invalid_host? is true whether or not the InvalidURIError rescue works. Stub embeddable_host to a real host so only the malformed URL can cause the rejection.

sugestoes.texto: The registered fallback provider throws UnsupportedOperationException when constructing EC parameters required by AbstractJWKParser. With authz-client as the only crypto provider, AuthzClient.create now installs this provider globally, so parsing a P-256, P-384, or P-521 JWK fails before ECDSA signature verification can run; AbstractJWKParser also requires getKeyFactory("ECDSA"), which this provider rejects. Implement EC parameter construction and EC key-factory lookup using the JDK APIs so the fallback supports the EC JWK parsing path.

readSequence accepts child encodings that extend past the sequence's declared content length. For example, 30 05 02 01 01 02 01 01 is accepted as two integers even though the second integer extends outside the five-byte sequence, and asn1derToConcatenatedRS consequently converts a malformed DER signature instead of rejecting it. Reject a child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length and require the remaining length to reach exactly zero.

The loop accepts a child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence content: subtraction makes length negative and the method returns successfully. For example, `30 04 02 01 01 02 01 01` declares four content bytes but contains two three-byte INTEGERs; readSequence returns both, and asn1derToConcatenatedRS accepts the malformed signature. Require each child to fit within the remaining sequence length (and reject a negative remainder), so bytes outside the declared sequence cannot become its members.

Reject a child whose encoded size exceeds the sequence's remaining content length. Currently, for example, `30 01 02 01 01` is accepted: the sequence declares one content byte, but readNext consumes the entire three-byte INTEGER, then length becomes -2 and the loop returns successfully. A sequence containing two integers can likewise be accepted with its declared length ending inside the second integer. This lets malformed signatures cross the enclosing ASN.1 boundary instead of producing an IOException.

Both sides of the assertion originate from the decoder under test. If asn1derToConcatenatedRS regressed to returning a zero-filled array of signLength, every test would still pass: encoding those zeros and decoding them again produces the same zeros. Assert that the reconstructed DER equals the original JCA DER signature, or verify the reconstructed signature against data and the public key, so lost or corrupted R/S values fail.

All three cases generate a default EC key (normally P-256); changing the signature hash to ES384/ES512 does not change the key's curve or the R/S sizes. Consequently testES512 still passes if long-form DER sequence length handling is broken, because its actual signature remains a short P-256 sequence, merely padded during conversion. Generate the matching P-256, P-384, or P-521 key inside the parameterized helper so each named case exercises its intended signature sizes.

The loop accepts a child even when its full encoding exceeds the remaining sequence length, then exits with a negative length and returns success. For example, `30 01 02 01 01` declares one content byte but returns the three-byte INTEGER as a valid sequence element. This makes the decoder return values that are not contained in the declared ASN.1 sequence. Reject an element whose encoded length exceeds the remaining content length.

All three tests generate the same default EC key (typically P-256). Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA changes the digest, not the key's curve, so the ES384 and ES512 cases merely pad P-256 components and never test real P-384/P-521 signatures. In particular, this misses the long-form DER sequence length encountered with P-521. Generate a key with an explicit curve corresponding to the algorithm inside test().

issues.descricao: concatenatedRSToASN1DER encodes r and s into two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances before re-encoding them in the return statement.
issues.textoGolden: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls allocate encoders and encode rBigInteger/sBigInteger, but their results are discarded — the returned DER comes entirely from the expression at lines 117-121, which re-encodes the same BigIntegers. These two statements have no effect and should be removed (they are a leftover from an earlier formulation).

Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` encode values and discard the results. The return expression re-encodes the same values, so these lines are dead computation left over from a copy-paste or refactor. Remove them.

issues.descricao: order() is added to CryptoProvider as an abstract method, breaking source and binary compatibility for existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations.
issues.textoGolden: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

comentarios.texto: order() was added as an abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes order() on every ServiceLoader-discovered CryptoProvider via Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Any CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface (an external or separately built provider jar on the classpath) will throw AbstractMethodError at detection time, i.e. during AuthzClient.create()/server bootstrap, before any provider is usable. Giving order() a default implementation (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) avoids the binary-incompatibility.

issues.descricao: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order() reversed and silently picks index 0, removing the previous multiple-providers error. WHY: Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so ambiguous classpath (e.g. default+FIPS) now nondeterministically picks one by ServiceLoader order instead of failing fast, risking wrong FIPS vs non-FIPS crypto. HOW: only auto-ignore lower-order providers; throw when the top two have equal order().

Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

detectProvider() no longer fails fast when multiple CryptoProviders are present and instead silently picks the first after sorting by order() descending. All Keycloak providers return the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200), so a tie between two providers is broken by the non-deterministic ServiceLoader iteration order rather than the intended priority. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException forcing the classpath to be corrected; now a deployment with two provider jars (exactly the 'multiple providers on classpath' scenario this PR enables) can silently select the unintended provider — e.g. a non-FIPS/strict provider when FIPS is required — with no error. Use a stable tie-breaker (delegate to the provider name/type) or reject equal top orders instead of relying on ServiceLoader order.

issues.descricao: Claims a wrong-length JOSE signature causes an unchecked exception in concatenatedRSToASN1DER; verifiers catch it and report verification failure, as with the existing providers.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature without validating signature.length==signLength. WHY: short JOSE input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and long input is silently truncated to signLength, breaking the ECDSACryptoProvider contract (IOException on malformed) used by verifier contexts. HOW: check length upfront and throw IOException.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER never validates signature.length == signLength before System.arraycopy(signature,0,r,1,len) / (signature,len,s,1,len). A short JWS signature throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, breaking verification on attacker-controlled input. Validate length and throw IOException.

issues.descricao: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.

comentarios.texto: Single default EC keypair reused for ES256/ES384/ES512: testES384/testES512 names claim larger curves but body signs with the same P-256 key and only pads to larger signLength, so full-width 384/521-bit handling is never exercised. Generate a per-algorithm keypair with the correct curve (e.g. secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) before signing.

Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

issues.descricao: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.

comentarios.texto: Tautological round-trip assertion: rsConcat2 is derived from rsConcat via encode+decode that are inverses if self-consistent, so assertArrayEquals(rsConcat,rsConcat2) passes even if both directions are wrong. Verify against external oracle: Signature.initVerify + verify(asn1Des) and/or compare rsConcat to expected split, not just to itself.

The test only checks self-consistency: it asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(g(asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign))) == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign), i.e. that concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a right inverse of asn1derToConcatenatedRS. It never compares against the original DER `sign`, never verifies the ECDSA signature, and never asserts the emvider output is canonical DER. Because the decoder it reads back with (ASN1Decoder.readLength) accepts non-canonical long-form lengths (e.g. 0x81) and validates only tag numbers, a regression in ASN1Encoder.writeLength that always emitted long form would still round-trip and the test would still pass, even though the produced signature would no longer be valid DER and would be rejected by the Keycloak server / a JDK Signature.verify. Assert the encoded signature is valid DER (e.g. verify it with a JDK Signature, or compare asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign) against a known-good width-padded r||s and assert its length equals algorithm.getSignatureLength()).

The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
issues.textoGolden: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

comentarios.texto: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default KeyStore provider (e.g. SUN) instead of a BouncyCastle provider, violating the method's contract ('@return BouncyCastle security provider'). This value is consumed by BouncyIntegration.loadProvider() (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:34) to set the static BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER name, so whenever this authz-client provider is the one selected by CryptoIntegration, every Keycloak code path that does getInstance(..., BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER) silently looks algorithms up in a non-BC provider (e.g. 'SUN'), which can produce failures or different crypto implementation than expected. Returning a provider that is not BouncyCastle while claiming to be the BouncyCastle provider makes BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER point to the wrong provider.

getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), i.e. the JDK default keystore provider (SUN), yet the method name and the CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() contract say it returns the BouncyCastle provider. A caller that uses the returned Provider as the BouncyCastle provider (to look up BC algorithms or to register it) will silently get the wrong (often already-registered) provider. Either return the actual BC provider or rename/document the method so the name matches what it returns.

WHAT: getBouncyCastleProvider returns KeyStore.getInstance(defaultType).getProvider() (e.g. SUN) as the BouncyCastle provider. WHY: BouncyIntegration.loadProvider caches this name for all Signature/Cipher/KeyFactory lookups, so standalone authz-client gets PROVIDER=SUN instead of BC/null and BC-specific algorithms/FIPS expectations break. HOW: return null like WildFlyElytronProvider does when no BC provider is available.

issues.descricao: Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
issues.textoGolden: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding 0x80 and callers pass it to new byte[length]. WHY: causes NegativeArraySizeException (unchecked) in readInteger/readNext instead of IOException, crashing signature-verification callers that expect checked failure on malformed DER. HOW: throw IOException for 0x80 since DER forbids indefinite lengths.

readInteger passes readLength() result directly to read(length)->new byte[length]. readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length 0x80, so a crafted INTEGER with length 0x80 throws unchecked NegativeArraySizeException at allocation instead of IOException. Reject length<0 here (indefinite length not valid for DER INTEGER).

readInteger() calls readLength(), which returns -1 for an indefinite-length element (first length byte 0x80). That -1 is passed straight to read(length) at line 72, which does `new byte[-1]` and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException, even though readInteger declares only IOException. The signature bytes fed to asn1derToConcatenatedRS come from an externally supplied ECDSA signature, so a malformed signature escapes as an unhandled runtime exception instead of the declared IOException. readLength()'s -1 branch is handled for sequences but not here; guard the negative/indefinite value (throw IOException) before calling read(length).

issues.descricao: Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: readSequence loops while(length>0) subtracting child TLV lengths but never verifies sum equals declared length nor rejects trailing bytes. WHY: lets overlong sequences and trailing garbage after the two integers be accepted as valid, diverging from strict BC ASN1InputStream and enabling signature malleability in the ECDSA verify path. HOW: enforce length==0 after loop and no remaining bytes in the outer buffer.

readSequence accepts a child whose encoded size exceeds the remaining declared sequence length. For example, `30 04 02 01 01 02 01 01` is accepted as a two-integer sequence even though its children occupy six bytes rather than the declared four, so asn1derToConcatenatedRS silently converts malformed DER instead of rejecting it. Restrict child decoding to the sequence's declared content boundary and throw IOException when a child exceeds the remaining length.

Bound each child TLV to the remaining sequence length before accepting it. Currently readNext() reads from the whole input and length may become negative, which silently ends the loop successfully. For example, `30 05 02 01 01 02 01 01` is accepted as a two-integer sequence although the second INTEGER crosses the declared sequence boundary. Decode through a stream limited to the sequence content, or reject a child whose encoded size exceeds the remaining length, so malformed DER cannot be converted as a valid signature.

issues.descricao: Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.

comentarios.texto: Reject INTEGER values that do not fit the requested component width instead of silently dropping their high bytes. Removing a single leading sign-padding zero is valid, but this branch also truncates actual magnitude bytes: a positive value 2^256 + 1 becomes 1 when qLength is 32. Thus DER-to-concatenated conversion can return a different signature from the one supplied. Validate nonnegative values and their bit length before padding or removing sign padding.

issues.descricao: Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

comentarios.texto: The newly registered client CryptoProvider does not satisfy the existing EC JWK parsing consumer: core's AbstractJWKParser calls createECParams(name) and getKeyFactory("ECDSA") to construct an EC public key, and both operations now throw UnsupportedOperationException when this provider is selected. Consequently, a standalone authz client using this provider cannot parse EC keys for ECDSA verification, even though signature conversion is implemented. Implement the JDK-backed curve-parameter and key-factory operations (mapping ECDSA to EC as needed), rather than leaving this existing consumer with an unsupported contract.

sugestoes.texto: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits four abstract members from StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing them. Accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector invokes this class in models/detector.py and raises TypeError, aborting process_detectors instead of preserving the previous no-op behavior. Keep this placeholder on DetectorHandler with an evaluate method returning an empty dict until the stateful methods are implemented.

Changing this empty class to inherit StatefulDetectorHandler makes it abstract: it implements neither get_dedupe_value nor get_group_key_values nor the newly required build_occurrence_and_event_data. When a metric-alert Detector's detector_handler property constructs the registered handler, Python raises TypeError before evaluation can run. Previously this handler was concrete and safely returned no results. Keep the concrete no-op handler until the stateful hooks are implemented, or implement all required hooks before switching the base class.

Changing this subclass to StatefulDetectorHandler makes it abstract: that base requires counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Unlike the updated test subclass, this class implements none of them. Instantiating the registered metric-alert detector handler will therefore raise TypeError rather than evaluating the packet. Keep the concrete no-op DetectorHandler implementation (returning an empty dictionary for the new evaluate contract) until the stateful methods are implemented.

Changing this concrete handler to StatefulDetectorHandler leaves get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly required build_occurrence_and_event_data abstract. Accessing Detector.detector_handler for the metric-alert group type therefore raises TypeError during handler construction, before process_detectors can evaluate it; previously this handler could be instantiated and returned an empty list. Keep the placeholder concrete with the updated dictionary evaluation contract until its stateful hooks are implemented.

The new occurrence test double ignores `value`, making the assertions insensitive to whether `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the actual measurement to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. In `test_state_results_multi_group`, group_2 has value 10 but the expected occurrence is built with 6, and the test still passes. A regression that passes a constant or reuses the first group's value therefore goes undetected. Include the value in the generated evidence data (and use 10 for the second expected occurrence), or assert the hook's arguments explicitly.

The docstring immediately below still says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but this change returns a dictionary keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Callers following that documentation and iterating the return value will get keys rather than evaluation results. Update the docstring to describe the mapping contract.

The preceding TODO says this will become a stateful detector when that abstraction is built, but the class now inherits that very abstraction. Remove or revise the TODO so readers are not told the stateful abstraction is still missing.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now stale. MetricAlertDetectorHandler already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler. Remove or reword the TODO.

Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here.
